Arundel's villa sits on the bank of the Rideau River, twenty minutes' drive south of the city center. Now that you're seeing it in person, it's hard to believe you ever forgot the sight of it. A lush garden occupies the front lawn and you can remember clear as day the roses waiting to bloom in the summer between manicured shrubs that lie covered tonight in a light dusting of snow. It will be months before the garden springs to life again, and yet you can see it as if it's blossomed just for you—a vision of rebirth after a long sleep in the cold earth.

The house itself isn't what you'd consider terribly ostentatious—it's not the Prince's primary residence after all—but by mortal standards it's quite lavish. Stone veneer has been arranged in a tasteful array of tans and off-whites framing elegant windows covered from the inside with blackout curtains. Large flagstones mark your progress as you walk from the driveway to the front door, passing between a set of almost rustic-looking red oak columns.

*page_break The Beast Rages
When the fever of bloodlust breaks and you come back to your senses, Trevor's mutilated body is nothing but a pile of rotten remains, staining your arms up to the elbows. He must have perished long before you stopped slashing, causing his body to revert to its natural age. You rise, standing on shaky legs as you tear free Trevor's coat jacket and use the remaining unsullied bits to wipe gore from your forearms. It's not a perfect job, but it will have to do for now. You grunt with satisfaction—luckily for you, you weren't wearing pristine white like he was.
